events.text:
## Recommendation
- Go to **Grand Haven** for the pier. My expected pier rating there is **2 (average)**.
- **St. Joseph** is a close second, also about **2 (average)**.
- Expect **1 (below average)** at **South Haven** and **Muskegon**.
- No report in the last four weeks describes pier fishing at any of these ports. Every rating here is my estimate, based on boat results.

## Why
- Grand Haven had the strongest boat report: the July 19 bulletin rated boat salmon fishing good (3), and the pier usually lags the boats.
- Muskegon and South Haven were both rated below average (1) for boats on July 19, so I'd expect the pier there to be slow too.
- St. Joseph boats were rated average (2) on July 19, and I'd expect the pier to land in the same range.

## Evidence
**Recent reports** (all boat reports; the newest is 2023-07-19, six days old):
- Grand Haven (2023-07-19): boats caught salmon and trout "65 to 120 feet down in 130 to 220 feet of water." Meat rigs and green flies worked; quality 3.
- Muskegon (2023-07-19): "hit or miss," best "60 to 100 feet down in 110 to 200 feet of water"; glow spoons and meat rigs; quality 1.
- South Haven (2023-07-19): boats had "mostly lake trout with some coho"; quality 1.
- St. Joseph (2023-07-19): "a few fish in 100 feet of water," slowing; quality 2.
- The July 5 reports were similar: South Haven and St. Joseph were fair to average, with fish deep and spoons working.

**Past seasons** (history, not current; similar buoy temperature of about 71-75 F):
- In early August 2022, St. Joseph boats rated good (3) and Muskegon good (3), while South Haven was slow-to-fair (1). (St. Joseph, 2022-08-03; Muskegon, 2022-08-03; South Haven, 2022-08-03)
- In mid-July 2022, Grand Haven and Muskegon were slow (0) for boats. (2022-07-14)

**Conditions now:**
- The latest buoy readings I have are from the week before today, not live: St. Joseph averaged 73 F (+3 F over the week), South Haven 73 F (+1 F), and Grand Haven and Muskegon 71 F (flat).
- I have no pierhead water temperature or upwelling signal for any port. Without that, I can't say whether cold water is moving toward the piers.
- General guidance (Michigan Sea Grant / MSU Extension): mature Chinook in early fall hold in water of 55 F or less, and north or east winds that cause upwelling bring salmon toward piers. Nothing in the data says whether that is happening this week.

## Caveats
- The newest report is six days old, and the conditions data is also a week old and from a buoy offshore, not the pier.
- No pier reports exist for these four ports in this window, so the pier ratings are my inference from boat results.
- Ratings are the reports' boat quality scores (0–4) converted to pier expectations; they are not DNR pier ratings.
- Check the pierhead temperature and wind before you go. A sharp drop in water temperature with north or east wind would favor the pier; if you see that, St. Joseph or Grand Haven should improve.

## Sources
- DNR bulletin, July 19 2023 (Grand Haven, Muskegon, South Haven, St. Joseph): https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/366250d
- DNR bulletin, July 5 2023 (South Haven, St. Joseph): https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/363ad03
- DNR bulletin, August 3 2022 (past season comparison): https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3268d0b
